label: <DEL> in long (L=8-9) sequences starting with j, boosted by m/z/r/o/l in the prefix
explanation: Fires only on the <DEL> step (100% of mass), almost only when L=9 (84% of mass) or L=8 (16%), i.e. right when the model is about to output original token 0. Strongly keyed on that first token being j (73% of mass, lift about 20x); smaller contributions when it is u/t/b. Within j-initial long sequences it fires more often and more strongly when the prefix contains several of m, z, r, o, l (the top examples look like j m r z m ..., j r z z l ...). Sequences that start with something other than j fire weakly, and only when they contain many m/z/r tokens. Never fires in the original or copy phases, or for L<=6. Precision is limited: most j-initial L>=8 sequences do not activate it, so it seems to behave like a sparse threshold on a combination of first-token identity and prefix content that a simple predicate only partly captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig2=z (+3.59), phase=1 & out_tok=j (+3.38), phase=1 & out_tok=u (+3.07), orig2=r (+3.06), orig2=m (+3.00), out_tok=j (+2.73). Lower it: orig7=- (-4.75), in_first=0 (-3.21), orig2=q (-2.07), orig1=c (-1.95).
